seoTitle: How to Restore a Deleted Microsoft Loop Page
metaDescription: Restore a deleted Microsoft Loop page from the workspace Recycle bin, find Loop components deleted in Teams or Outlook, and what an admin can do if a whole workspace was deleted.
intro:
A page deleted inside a Loop workspace goes to that workspace's Recycle bin, and restoring it takes three clicks. The harder cases are the ones the Loop app doesn't cover: a Loop component that lived in a Teams chat or an Outlook email, or an entire workspace that someone deleted.

Where a piece of Loop content is stored depends on where it was created, and that decides which recycle bin it lands in. This guide starts with the workspace bin, then shows where to look for everything else, including the admin route for deleted workspaces that Microsoft's end-user help says can't be restored.

tables.title: Where deleted Loop content goes
rows: Loop app workspace (shared or My workspace)
The workspace's own Recycle bin in Loop
Teams private chat or private meeting
tables.note: Storage locations from Microsoft's "Overview of Loop storage" admin article, checked September 2026. Teams chat notes and Teams channel workspaces are stored in SharePoint Embedded containers, like Loop app workspaces.

steps.heading: Open the workspace the page was in
steps.body: Go to loop.cloud.microsoft and sign in. The home screen lists your workspaces as cards, each showing when it was last opened. Open the one that held the deleted page.

image.caption: The Loop home screen listing workspaces as cards, each with the time it was last opened.

steps.heading: Open Recycle bin at the bottom of the sidebar
steps.body: The left sidebar lists the workspace's pages under "Sorted by hierarchy". Scroll past the last page and Recycle bin sits on its own at the very bottom. You can open it from any page in the workspace.

image.caption: A workspace sidebar with pages under "Sorted by hierarchy" and the Recycle bin link at the bottom.

steps.heading: Restore the page
steps.body:
Find the page in the Recycle bin, select More (the three dots) and choose Restore. It goes back into the workspace's page list.

Stay away from Empty all at the top of the Recycle bin page. It clears everything in the bin, and Microsoft's help doesn't offer a way back for items removed that way.

steps.heading: Not in the workspace bin? Check where it was created
steps.body:
If the "page" was a Loop component shared in Teams or Outlook, it never lived in a Loop workspace, so it won't be in that bin. Use the table above to find its home.

Components from a Teams private chat, private meeting, Outlook email, OneNote or Whiteboard are files in the creator's OneDrive. Open onedrive.com with your work account, select Recycle bin, pick the file and click Restore. Work and school OneDrive keeps deleted files for 93 days unless your administrator changed that setting. If someone else created the component, it's in their OneDrive, not yours, and Microsoft notes that items shared with you can't be restored from your own recycle bin. Ask the creator to restore it. Components from a Teams channel or channel meeting are stored on the team's SharePoint site, so check that site's recycle bin.

steps.heading: If the whole workspace was deleted, ask an admin
steps.body:
Microsoft's Loop help is blunt about this: once deleted, workspaces can't be restored from the Loop app. An administrator may still be able to recover it. Loop workspaces are SharePoint Embedded containers, and an admin with the SharePoint Embedded Administrator or Global Administrator role can open the SharePoint admin center, expand SharePoint Embedded, choose Deleted containers, select the workspace and click Restore. It reappears under Active containers when the background job finishes.

Timing matters. Deleted containers are purged permanently after 93 days unless a retention policy says otherwise, and an admin can also permanently delete one sooner.

faq.question: Can I restore a deleted Loop workspace myself?
faq.answer: No. Microsoft's Loop help says deleted workspaces can't be restored from the app. An admin can restore the underlying container from the SharePoint admin center within 93 days.

faq.question: Is there one Recycle bin for all of Loop?
faq.answer: Not in the app. The Recycle bin link sits in each workspace's sidebar, so open it inside the workspace the page was deleted from.

faq.question: How long do I have to restore a Loop component from Teams chat?
faq.answer: Components from a private chat are OneDrive files, and work or school OneDrive keeps deleted files for 93 days unless your admin changed the setting.

faq.question: What does Empty all do?
faq.answer: It clears every item from that workspace's Recycle bin. Restore anything you need first.
